jobs.title: Director Of Development
jobs.description:
**DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT AND MAJOR GIFTS**

 **Status**: FT Exempt

**Reports To:** Chief Executive Officer

**Schedule of Hours:** Monday – Friday, 9\-5 with occasional evenings and weekends

**Possible Percentage of Work from Home:** 50% or more onsite

**Mandated Reporter:** No

 **ABOUT CORA**


CORA (Community Overcoming Relationship Abuse) is the only agency in San Mateo County solely focused on serving people experiencing intimate partner abuse. CORA provides comprehensive services including a 24\-hour hotline, emergency shelter, legal services, counseling, community education, and prevention programming. CORA is a multicultural agency committed to serving individuals regardless of age, ethnicity, race, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, immigration status, religion, financial status, language, or mental or physical ability.

**THE POSITION**


The Director of Development and Major Gifts leads CORA’s development department and is responsible for achieving an annual fundraising goal of approximately $3 million. The Director sets departmental priorities, establishes measurable goals, manages and develops staff, and uses fundraising data to evaluate performance and guide strategy.


This is a high\-touch fundraising leadership role with significant personal responsibility for major donor cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship. The Director manages a portfolio of approximately 140 major gift prospects and donors, builds the major donor pipeline, develops corporate and community partnerships, and leads strategies to increase donor acquisition, retention, and upgrades, including planned giving.


The Director works closely with the CEO, Board members, Board Development Committee, CFO, and development and marketing teams to strengthen CORA’s fundraising capacity and long\-term financial sustainability.

**PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Development Department Leadership**

* Lead, supervise, coach, and develop a team of three development staff who oversee foundations portfolio, special events, individual giving and marketing and communications.
* Establish departmental goals, priorities, work plans, and performance expectations.
* Monitor results, use data to identify gaps and opportunities, and hold staff accountable for measurable goals.
* Oversee the development budget and department systems, including donor management and tracking platforms.
* Partner with the CEO/CFO on vendors, consultants, and technology that strengthen development capacity.
**Major Gifts**

* Manage and grow a portfolio of approximately 140 major gift prospects and donors through face\-to\-face and virtual meetings, calls, solicitations, and personalized stewardship.
* Build and manage a strong major donor pipeline through prospect identification, research, qualification, cultivation, and solicitation.
* Develop strategies to increase donor acquisition, retention, and upgrades.
* Strengthen long\-term relationships with major donors and provide meaningful opportunities for engagement.
**Corporate \& Community Partnerships**

* Develop and implement strategies for corporate giving and sponsorships.
* Identify and cultivate businesses, corporate leaders, and community partners whose interests align with CORA’s mission.
* Personally cultivate and steward high\-value relationships and participate in solicitations.
**Development Strategy \& Campaigns**

* Develop and execute an integrated annual strategic plan across major gifts, individual giving, foundations, corporations, sponsorships, community partnerships, events, and campaigns.
* Use donor data, analytics, pipeline information, and campaign results to evaluate performance and refine strategy.
* Establish and monitor key development metrics and benchmarks.
* Create new initiatives to increase donor acquisition, retention, repeat giving, and overall fundraising capacity.
* Plan and oversee annual and special campaigns, for example, End of Year and Giving Tuesday.
**Special Events**

* Oversee fundraising events with revenue, donor acquisition, cultivation, and stewardship goals.
* Develop donor\-focused and VIP opportunities in collaboration with the development team.
* Evaluate event results and incorporate lessons learned into future strategy.
**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Minimum of 5–7 years of progressive experience in fundraising, donor cultivation, major gifts, nonprofit development, or a related field.
* Close ties to the local Peninsula and Bay Area community and businesses, strongly preferred.
* Bachelor’s degree required; advanced degree preferred.
* Demonstrated success by increasing fundraising revenue and achieving measurable goals. This includes experience personally cultivating, soliciting, and stewarding major donors, including donors capable of making gifts of $10,000 or more.
* Experience developing corporate donors, sponsors, and/or community partnerships that generate financial support.
* Experience managing fundraising campaigns and events.
* Experience leading, coaching, and managing development staff to achieve department goals.
* Strong CRM and donor data management skills.
* Ability to use donor and fundraising data to evaluate performance, identify opportunities, and inform development strategy.
* Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal, and relationship\-building skills, with the ability to engage donors, corporate leaders, and community partners.
* Nonprofit leadership experience preferred.
* CFRE credential preferred.
* Passion for and commitment to work addressing the impact of Intimate Partner Abuse.

**WORK ENVIRONMENT/ PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

* Ability to be onsite meeting donors and attending community events in San Mateo County weekly, required.
* Successful results upon hire from a DOJ Live Scan fingerprint clearance are required
* Completion of the 40 Hour Training – required and will be provided to the successful applicant upon hire if not already completed within last 5 years.
* Driver’s License and active

* Excellent interpersonal skills.
* Demonstrated commitment to social justice.
* Bilingual (Spanish/English) preferred.

**About The New York Climate Exchange**  

The New York Climate Exchange (“The Exchange”) is a global nonprofit organization dedicated to accelerating climate solutions through research, education, innovation, and collaboration. Through partnerships spanning academia, government, philanthropy, industry, and communities, The Exchange is building a world\-class climate solutions center headquartered in New York City.  

The Exchange brings together leading experts, practitioners, policymakers, and innovators to advance climate action and create scalable solutions for a more sustainable future.  

  

**Position Summary**  

The New York Climate Exchange seeks an exceptional Senior Executive Assistant (SEA) to serve as a trusted partner to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO).  

This is a highly visible and impactful role that extends well beyond traditional executive support. The Senior Executive Assistant is responsible for ensuring the CEO’s time, communications, priorities, stakeholder relationships, meetings, and travel are managed with precision, professionalism, and exceptional attention to detail. The role incorporating some of the capabilities commonly associated with a Chief of Staff, including executive operations, stakeholder management and communications support.  

The ideal candidate is a seasoned executive support professional with significant experience supporting CEOs, Presidents, Executive Directors, Founders, or similarly senior leaders. This individual operates with discretion, sound judgment, emotional intelligence, and a high degree of independence. The successful candidate will be highly organized, exceptionally resourceful, proactive, responsive, and comfortable working in an entrepreneurial, fast\-paced environment where priorities evolve rapidly.  

This individual will regularly engage with board members, major donors, philanthropists, government officials, academic partners, corporate leaders, community partners, and other high\-profile external stakeholders. The position requires flexibility and responsiveness, including periodic evening and weekend availability and the ability to manage urgent issues that arise outside traditional business hours.

**Stakeholder \& Relationship Management*** Serve as a key point of contact for internal and external stakeholders on behalf of the CEO.

jobs.description:
The Opportunity

The Sexual Violence Resource Center of the Bluegrass is seeking an experienced, mission\-driven Executive Director to provide strategic leadership and advance the organization's mission, financial sustainability, and community impact.

The Executive Director will lead the organization into its next chapter by strengthening organizational culture, developing and empowering leaders, and significantly advancing fundraising and resource\-development efforts. A critical priority is strengthening and diversifying the organization's funding base through donor and funder relationships, new revenue opportunities, and active Board and community engagement.

The successful candidate will be collaborative, accessible, emotionally intelligent, accountable, and comfortable serving as a highly visible external champion for the organization. How results are achieved is as important as the results themselves.

Key Responsibilities

* Provide strategic leadership and direction consistent with the organization's mission, values, and priorities.
* Lead the organization's fundraising and resource\-development strategy, with accountability for strengthening and diversifying revenue.
* Personally cultivate, solicit, and steward relationships with individual donors, foundations, corporations, government funders, and other funding partners.
* Identify and pursue new funding opportunities and partnerships that support long\-term financial sustainability.
* Engage and support the Board of Directors in fundraising, donor cultivation, community connections, and organizational advocacy.
* Serve as a visible and compelling ambassador with donors, community partners, policymakers, media, and other stakeholders.
* Build and sustain a healthy, respectful, collaborative, and accountable organizational culture.
* Lead, coach, and develop the leadership team while empowering directors to lead their respective areas of expertise.
* Partner with the Board on strategy, governance, organizational priorities, and long\-term sustainability.
* Maintain executive oversight of financial performance, budgeting, compliance, risk, and operations.
* Ensure programs and services remain mission\-aligned, survivor\-centered, trauma\-informed, effective, and responsive to community needs.
* Lead organizational change with transparency, appropriate employee engagement, and sound judgment.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant professional experience.
* Minimum of seven years of progressively responsible leadership experience, preferably within a nonprofit, human services, advocacy, health care, community\-based, or similarly mission\-driven organization.
* Demonstrated success in fundraising and resource development, including cultivating funders and donors, securing financial support, and developing or executing fundraising strategies.
* Experience developing new funding opportunities and strengthening or diversifying organizational revenue.
* Demonstrated success leading and developing teams, preferably including managers or functional leaders.
* Experience with organizational budgeting, financial oversight, strategic planning, and resource allocation.
* Experience working effectively with a Board and engaging Board members in fundraising, community relationships, and organizational strategy.
* Strong interpersonal, public communication, relationship\-building, and decision\-making skills.
* Demonstrated ability to build trust, navigate conflict constructively, receive feedback, and lead through organizational change.
* Commitment to the organization's mission and the individuals and communities it serves.

Preferred Qualifications

* Master's degree in a relevant field.
* Nonprofit executive or senior leadership experience.
* Experience with major gifts, foundation relationships, government grants, corporate partnerships, fundraising campaigns, and donor stewardship.
* Experience leading organizational or cultural change.
* Familiarity with trauma\-informed organizations, advocacy, sexual violence services, behavioral health, or related human services.

Direct clinical experience is not required. The Executive Director must be able to support and empower qualified subject\-matter leaders responsible for the organization's specialized services.

Pay: $95,000\.00 \- $115,000\.00 per year

Work Location: In person

jobs.description:
**Community Missions Corporation \- St. Joseph, MO**

Founded in 2004 as a nonprofit, 501(c)(3\) organization, Community Missions Corporation strives to eliminate chronic homelessness in Northwest Missouri. CMC provides permanent housing for chronically homeless individuals in St. Joseph and Buchanan County Missouri. We believe in the power of community. Our programs are designed to uplift individuals and families, providing necessary resources and support.

**Programs Operating Today**

**Haven House:** St. Joseph's Haven opened its doors on September 9, 2009, to an eagerly awaiting throng of men. St. Joseph's Haven houses 18 chronically homeless men in 9 semi\-private suites. “The Haven” also incorporates a "Safe Haven" component into its repertoire of services, providing shelter for up to 7 additional men during crisis situations.

**Juda House:** Juda House provides housing to sixteen (16\) chronically homeless men who are diagnosed with one or more disabilities. Case managers at Community Missions work to assure that the basic needs of each man in our care are met so that he can then begin addressing those issues that have rendered him homeless time and time again\- things like serious mental illness, alcohol and drug addiction, physical impairment.

**24 Hour Emergency Shelter \- My Brother's House:** Community Missions’ 24\-Hour Shelter provides a safe, supportive environment for both men and women experiencing homelessness in St. Joseph and the surrounding area. Unlike traditional shelters with limited hours, our facility is open around the clock, ensuring guests have consistent access to shelter, meals, restrooms, and basic needs every day of the year.

**Executive Director \- Job Description**

The Executive Director serves as the Chief Operations Officer of Community Missions Corporation and is responsible for the overall leadership, supervision, daily operations, strategic planning, program oversight, and organizational compliance. The Executive Director ensures the organization's mission is fulfilled by providing strong operational leadership, maintaining quality services, supporting staff development, and fostering community partnerships.

Because Community Missions Corp. programs operate 24/7, the Executive Director is expected to ensure that the needs of our programs are being met continuously. This may require attention to staff and programming outside of typical business hours.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**

* The Executive Director reports directly to the Board of Directors.
* Oversee progress, growth, and operations of CMC programs and initiatives.
* Develop and maintain a strong knowledge of issues surrounding homelessness, related services and community resources.
* Ensure safety of all staff and program participants.
* Maintain partnership with the Board of Directors and community stakeholders to address current needs and trends related to homelessness.
* Perform administrative and financial duties necessary to support the continued operation and growth of CMC.
* Seek, secure, and manage funding sources, including but not limited to grants.
* Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local regulations.
* Maintain document control and policy updates.
* Attend community meetings and build collaborative relationships with outside entities as an ambassador for Community Missions.
* Direct supervision of all program staff, Shelter Leads, Care Coordinators, Outreach staff, Case Managers, Peer Support staff, volunteers, and interns.
* All other duties as deemed necessary. These inclusions are descriptive, not exhaustive.

**Knowledge, Skills \& Abilities**

* Collaborative leadership approach within the organization and community.
* Conflict resolution and crisis intervention.
* Strong decision\-making and problem\-solving skills.

**Qualifications \& Requirements**

* Full\-time, salaried position.
* Duties performed on\-site and off\-site.
* Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
* Bachelor's degree required in a related competency; Master's degree preferred.
* Leadership experience in nonprofit management or public administration, healthcare, human services, or other related fields.

Pay: $75,000\.00 \- $95,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Paid time off
* Retirement plan

Work Location: In person

Most importantly, you'll have the chance to make a real and measurable impact on the lives of Hoosiers across Indiana.

  

**About the Indiana Department of Workforce Development (DWD):**
  

Our mission is to develop a premier workforce that will allow Indiana employers to flourish and entice businesses from outside our state to relocate to Indiana. Everyone at DWD will be required to think outside\-the\-box; to determine metrics that will allow for measurement and improvement and efficiencies to be made along the way. The Indiana Commission of Service \& Volunteerism (Serve Indiana) is housed within the Indiana Department of Workforce Development. Serve Indiana mobilizes people and resources to deliver creative solutions to community problems. The position requires a commitment to work alongside the DPA Officers, Executive Committee, State Committee, elected officials, and candidates across the state. **Summary:** The Chief Operating Officer (COO) serves as a key member of the executive leadership team and is responsible for providing strategic leadership, operational oversight, and organizational direction for the delivery of services across the organization. Reporting to the Chief Executive Officer, the COO ensures that operational programs are effectively managed, mission\-focused, financially responsible, and aligned with the values and traditions of the Franciscan mission.


The COO provides leadership for a broad range of service areas ensuring the highest standards of quality, safety, compliance, and person\-centered care are maintained across approximately 40 licensed long\-term care and community\-based facilities throughout Southeastern Wisconsin and Northern Illinois and three\-day program centers. Position resides at our headquarters in Jefferson, WI.


The successful candidate will be a collaborative and strategic leader who understands the complexities of human services, healthcare operations, and mission\-driven organizations. The COO will inspire teams, strengthen operational excellence, and lead continuous improvement initiatives that enhance the lives of the individuals served.


Requirements:
**Required Competencies**

**Mission\-Driven \& Faith\-Based Leadership:** Demonstrates commitment to St. Coletta’s Code of Conduct and Franciscan Values while modeling servant leadership, integrity, compassion, stewardship, and respect for the dignity of every individual.

**Strategic \& Organizational Leadership:** Ability to translate organizational strategy into action, lead continuous improvement initiatives, drive innovation, and strengthen policies, procedures, and operational effectiveness.

**Operational Excellence \& Business Acumen:** Demonstrates the ability to oversee complex operations, evaluate organizational performance, manage resources effectively, and support financial sustainability through sound decision\-making.

**Collaborative Leadership \& Relationship Building:** Builds strong partnerships across departments, service lines, and external stakeholders while fostering collaboration, trust, and alignment toward shared goals.

**Leadership Development \& Talent Management:** Develops high\-performing leaders through coaching, mentoring, accountability, and succession planning.

**Change Management \& Problem Solving:** Leads organizational change, responds effectively to complex challenges and crises, and implements innovative solutions that improve quality, safety, and service outcomes.

**Financial \& Data\-Driven Decision Making:** Understands budgeting processes, financial performance, and operational metrics; uses data and insights to guide priorities and achieve organizational goals.

**Communication \& Executive Presence:** Demonstrates exceptional communication, interpersonal skills, and professional judgment when engaging employees, leadership teams, the Board, residents, clients, families, community partners, and regulatory agencies.

**Regulatory, Quality \& Risk Management:** Maintains understanding of applicable regulations, compliance requirements, quality improvement practices, and risk management strategies.

**Accountability, Integrity \& Adaptability:** Maintains confidentiality, demonstrates ethical decision\-making, manages competing priorities effectively, and adapts to evolving organizational needs.

**Essential Duties and Responsibilities**Include the following and other duties as assigned. **Executive Leadership**


Serve as a strategic partner to the Chief Executive Officer in advancing the organization's mission, vision, values, and long\-term strategic goals.


Model and promote the organization's faith\-based mission, vision, and values in all aspects of leadership and decision\-making.


Provide executive oversight of all operational departments, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and financial sustainability.


Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation, and servant leadership throughout the organization.


Develop, mentor, and evaluate senior leaders while building leadership capacity and succession plans across the organization.


Lead organizational change initiatives that strengthen operations, improve outcomes, and support long\-term growth.

**Operational Management**


Direct and oversee day\-to\-day operations across residential housing, day programs, transportation, maintenance \& facilities, admissions, case management and nursing services.


Ensure operational consistency, quality, and service excellence across all programs.


Evaluate operational performance and implement best practices to improve efficiency, resident and client satisfaction, and organizational effectiveness.


Lead continuous quality improvement initiatives focused on operational excellence and exceptional customer experiences.


Ensure appropriate staffing models and operational resources are in place to meet organizational objectives.

**Financial Stewardship**


Partner with the Chief Financial Officer to develop and manage annual operating and capital budgets.


Monitor financial performance, labor productivity, occupancy, census, and operational expenses to ensure long\-term sustainability.


Support capital planning, facility improvements, and long\-range financial strategies.


Quality, Compliance \& Risk Management


Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations, including CMS, Wisconsin DHS, Illinois DHS, HUD, and other governing agencies, as applicable.


Maintain survey readiness and oversee quality assurance and regulatory compliance activities.


Lead organizational risk management, emergency preparedness, and business continuity

Since 2000, Crum \& Forster’s Accident \& Health division (A\&H) has offered a diverse portfolio of specialty insurance and reinsurance products nationwide. We place a strong focus on product development and creative distribution methods, along with excellent client service and support.  

In addition to our robust domestic portfolio, which spans both special risk and medical solutions, A\&H works on an international basis through various partnerships. Our global capabilities provide our partners with even broader flexibility in underwriting solutions.  

The qualities and capabilities of Crum \& Forster Accident \& Health demonstrate our philosophy of building meaningful, long\-term partnerships and our dedication to providing alternative strategies in an ever\-changing insurance market.

**Duties**
----------


The Deputy Directorate Head is responsible for directing and supervising the overall structure and effectiveness of the Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP), in accordance with the NSF Strategic Plan and Agency priorities.

The incumbent works collaboratively with the Assistant Director, Directorate Head, and the Chief of Business Operations. jobs.title: Chief Development Officer
jobs.description:
**About Encircle**



Encircle exists to bring families and communities together to enable LGBTQ\+ youth to thrive.

  

Since opening our first home in Provo, Utah, Encircle has grown into a statewide organization serving thousands of LGBTQ\+ youth, young adults, families, and community members each year through mental health services, community programming, friendship, and connection.

  

Across our homes and therapy services, Encircle creates spaces where LGBTQ\+ young people can build meaningful relationships, access affirming mental health care, and feel supported by the people and communities around them.

  

What can sometimes be missed about Encircle is that our work is not only about supporting LGBTQ\+ youth, it is also about strengthening families and communities. Our approach, No Sides, Only Love, is built around creating places where people with different backgrounds, beliefs, and experiences can come together around a shared commitment to helping young people thrive.

  

We are now looking for an experienced development leader to help build the fundraising strategy, relationships, and team that will sustain and expand that work for years to come.

 **Why Utah**



This role is based in the Salt Lake City area and offers the opportunity to live and work in one of the country's fastest\-growing regions. Utah combines a thriving business and philanthropic community with easy access to world\-class outdoor recreation, including skiing, hiking, biking, and national parks. Salt Lake City has a growing arts, food, sports, and cultural scene, an international airport minutes from downtown, and a strong network of business, nonprofit, and community leaders.

  

For candidates relocating to Utah, this role offers a unique opportunity to become deeply connected to a growing philanthropic community while helping shape the future of an organization with statewide and potentially national impact.

 **Job Summary**



Encircle is seeking an experienced, strategic, and hands\-on Chief Development Officer to lead and grow our fundraising efforts. The CDO will be responsible for developing and executing the fundraising strategy. Within that broader goal, the CDO will personally own and grow a portfolio of major and principal donors expected to generate $3 million in annual philanthropic revenue.

  

Working directly with the CEO, the CDO will build on Encircle's strong existing donor base by taking ownership of key donor relationships, deepening those partnerships, and developing new relationships with major and principal donors. The CDO will shape Encircle's long\-term fundraising strategy, expand the major\-gift pipeline, and partner closely with Marketing, Finance, the Board, and organizational leadership.

  

The CDO will initially lead a lean Development team, directly managing Encircle's Development Manager, who oversees grants and supports development operations. As fundraising grows and performance goals are achieved, the CDO will have the opportunity to design and build the Development team and infrastructure needed to support Encircle's next stage of growth.

  

This is a highly hands\-on leadership role for someone equally comfortable setting strategy and doing the work required to achieve it. The ideal candidate can move seamlessly between developing a multi\-year revenue strategy, sitting across the table from a major donor, analyzing pipeline performance, strengthening fundraising systems, and building organizational fundraising capacity.

 **Key Responsibilities**


**Fundraising Strategy \& Leadership**


* Develop and execute a comprehensive annual and multi\-year fundraising strategy.
* Establish clear fundraising priorities, revenue targets, pipeline expectations, and performance metrics.
* Regularly analyze fundraising results and pipeline performance to identify opportunities, risks, and areas requiring additional focus.
* Develop a thoughtful plan for expanding the Development team and investing in additional fundraising capacity as revenue milestones are achieved.
* Partner closely with the CEO, Board, Marketing, and Finance leadership on fundraising strategy and organizational priorities.


**Major \& Principal Gifts**


* Personally own and manage a portfolio of major and principal donor relationships expected to generate approximately $3 million in annual philanthropic revenue.
* Develop individualized strategies for donor identification, qualification, cultivation, solicitation, renewal, and increased giving.
* Personally cultivate, solicit, and close six\- and seven\-figure philanthropic gifts.
* Identify and develop new high\-capacity donor prospects through research, referrals, community relationships, Board connections, and strategic outreach.
* Conduct and apply donor prospect research using public tax filings, wealth indicators, philanthropic giving history, and other publicly available information.


**Donor Stewardship \& Engagement**


* Ensure major donors receive thoughtful, timely, and highly personalized communication, recognition, and stewardship.
* Strengthen Encircle's overall donor stewardship strategy in partnership with Marketing.
* Create a consistent and meaningful donor experience across communications, campaigns, events, impact reporting, tours, and recognition.


**External Relations \& Partnerships**


* Represent Encircle in donor meetings, tours, community events, and other external engagement opportunities.
* Develop and cultivate high\-value corporate, foundation, and community partnerships with meaningful philanthropic potential.
* Engage Board members and volunteer leaders in donor introductions, cultivation, solicitation, and stewardship.
* Build and strengthen relationships across Utah's philanthropic, corporate, and nonprofit communities.

jobs.description:

====================================================================

The principal activity of the Assistant Director of Development is to be externally focused, with responsibility for engaging a portfolio of individuals, corporations, and foundations that have a potential affinity with ASU. The Assistant Director’s effectiveness will be evaluated on the ability to achieve financial goals and contact metrics consistent with the programs and prospects assigned.


**What you’ll do**

* Create fundraising and engagement efforts for the W. P. Carey School of Business Department of Information Systems, including the Center for **AI and Data Analytics** . These efforts help advance the ASU Charter through philanthropy.
* In a team approach with the Director of Development at the W. P. Carey School of Business, create fundraising and engagement efforts for three W. P. Carey School of Business areas, which include, but are not limited to: Department of Marketing, Department of Management and Entrepreneurship, and The School of Technology, Innovation, and Entrepreneurship (T.I.E.)

* Two (2\) to (3\) years of successful development experience or transferrable experience
* Demonstrated ability in securing major grants and gifts from individuals, corporations, foundations, and other private funding sources
* Demonstrated organizational skills and experience in managing events and other complex activities in support of development objectives

**Preferred education and experience**

* Two (2\) to (3\) years of successful development experience in higher education or transferrable experience

**The ASU Foundation** fosters partnerships between ASU and like\-minded individuals, corporations and foundations who believe in ASU’s mission and provide resources for ASU to manifest its charter into meaningful impact. **At the ASU Foundation we value**

**Character**  

We prioritize character and integrity in every decision and action, establishing trust as the foundation of all that we do.

jobs.title: Deputy Director, Network + Engagement
jobs.description:
Georgetown University comprises two unique campuses in the nation’s capital. With the Hilltop Campus located in the heart of the historic Georgetown neighborhood, and the Capitol Campus, just minutes from the U.S. Capitol and U.S. Supreme Court, Georgetown University offers rigorous academic programs, a global perspective, and unparalleled opportunities to engage with Washington, D.C. Our community is a close\-knit group of remarkable individuals driven by intellectual inquiry, a commitment to social justice, and a shared dedication to making a difference in the world.

**Requirements**

**Job Overview**

  

The Beeck Center for Social Impact \+ Innovation at Georgetown University is dedicated to improving how people experience government by strengthening the design and delivery of public services. As a nonprofit, nonpartisan center, we catalyze cross\-sector collaboration to advance people\-first, digitally\-enabled approaches through applied research, peer learning, and hands\-on support—helping government deliver better outcomes for communities.

  

The Beeck Center is seeking a Deputy Director, Network \+ Engagement to provide operational leadership and deep subject matter expertise to our growing network portfolio. In this role, you will lead the management and growth of the State Chief Data Officers (CDO) Network, providing strategic direction and comprehensive program oversight for one of the Digital Government Network’s flagship communities of practice.

  

Additionally, the Deputy Director serves as a trusted connector across the broader Beeck Center ecosystem. You will foster deep collaboration and cross\-functional synergy between the Digital Government Network and the Center’s research, training, and technical assistance functions to advance shared organizational goals. As a member of the network team, you will contribute directly to the strategic development and operational management of the Digital Government Network—supporting network expansion, program innovation, and the continuous identification of new opportunities to increase member value and deliver long\-term impact.

  

This position is ideal for a relationship\-driven, operationally excellent professional who is passionate about cultivating communities of practice, building high\-trust networks, and supporting public sector leaders utilizing data and technology to serve the public.

  

Before submitting your application to Georgetown University, visit the Beeck Center’s careers page to learn more about the recruiting process, timeline, and supplemental application requirements.

 **Work Interactions**


The Deputy Director, Network \+ Engagement will be a core member of the network portfolio team and report to a Senior Director within the Digital Government Network. The Deputy Director will work closely with other network team members, including peer network managers, technical assistance providers, and program staff. This role demands substantial external engagement, serving as a primary point of contact for State Chief Data Officers, senior government officials, philanthropic partners, and ecosystem stakeholders. Internally, the Deputy Director will routinely collaborate across matrixed teams, partnering with Research, Training \+ Technical Assistance, Communications, and Operations functions, and will have the opportunity to manage or mentor staff, contractors, or Student Analysts.

 **Requirements and Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree and 5\-7 years of relevant leadership experience, with a clear focus on program management, capacity building, developing communities of practice, or network facilitation (each year of relevant work experience may be substituted for each year of required education).
* Experience working in state, federal, or local government agencies—specifically within an enterprise\-level data office, digital service team, or IT governance structure.
* Demonstrated experience establishing, directing, and expanding multi\-stakeholder peer\-learning networks, professional associations, or collaborative public sector cohorts.
* Deep knowledge of public sector data landscapes, data governance, data management, emerging government technology, or digital service delivery frameworks.
* Exceptional relationship management and interpersonal skills, with a proven history of serving as a trusted advisor to executive\-level data leaders and government practitioners.
* Knowledge of common data analytics tools (e.g., SQL, Python, Tableau), cloud data infrastructure, and data management vendors.
* Advanced oral and written communication skills, including experience designing meeting agendas, facilitating high\-stakes group discussions, authoring data publications (e.g., playbooks, toolkits, research reports), and writing program documentation for professional audiences.
* Strong project management skills, including experience using technology and digital platforms (e.g., Asana, Slack, Airtable, SugarCRM/Salesforce, Google Workspace) to run operations within a matrixed or distributed environment.
* Experience managing or mentoring team members, contractors, or student analysts.
* Preferred Qualifications
* Master’s degree in Public Policy or related field, with a focus on data.
* Proven experience scaling or expanding professional networks, including evaluating member engagement metrics and introducing new programming innovations.
* Familiarity with human\-centered design principles, agile project management, or public sector equity practices.

 **Work Mode Designation**


This position has been designated as Remote. Please note that work mode designations are regularly reviewed in order to meet the evolving needs of the University. Such review may necessitate a change to a position’s mode of work designation. Complete details about Georgetown University’s mode of work designations for staff positions can be found on the Department of Human Resources website: https://hr.georgetown.edu/mode\-of\-work\-

new_jobs.description:
**DOLORES HUERTA FOUNDATION (DHF)**


JOB DESCRIPTION


Job Title

  

Deputy Director

  

Department

  

Administration

  

Reports To

  

Executive Director

  

Location

  

DHF Headquarters – Bakersfield, CA

  

FLSA Status

  

Exempt

  

Pay Range

  

$160,000

  

Start Date

  

October 3rd or 5th, 2026

  

Supervisory Responsibility

  

Direct: Yes (Department Managers) \| Indirect: Yes (All Staff)

  

Date Approved

  

9/9/2026

  

Last Revised

  

9/9/2026

 **JOB SUMMARY**


The Deputy Director will be responsible for the day to day operational management of the DHF as well as coordinate training, orientation, and leadership development of staff and volunteers. The Deputy Director will work closely with the Executive Director and the senior management team to oversee the development and implementation of DHF’s strategic and operational plans. The Deputy Director will also serve as a strategic partner to the Executive Director on select development, communication, and organizational initiatives alongside the department leads responsible for those functions.

**ESSENTIAL DUTIES \& RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Overall responsibility for the day to day operation of the DHF.
* Coordinate training, orientation, and leadership development of staff and volunteers.
* Coordinate and plan regularly scheduled staff and management meetings, department/team meetings, training, and retreats.
* Coordinate strategic and operational planning in conjunction with DHF's planning consultant, staff and board.
* Ensure the development and implementation of action plans to maximize program results and effectiveness across all departments and organizational teams.
* Provide support to department managers and team leads to ensure implementation of organizational and departmental operational plans.
* Provide regular oversight to ensure actualization of goals, performance and accountability measurements, and reporting systems.
* Oversee implementation of programs, grant compliance, budgeting, and reporting.
* Assist managers with the evaluation of team members.
* Serve as mentor, coach, and guide to management staff.
* Implement a professional development program to address employee experience and skill gaps based on individual staff evaluations in conjunction with their supervisor.
* Assess DHF's participation in various coalitions and create criteria for joining new coalitions.
* Support DHF's fundraising and communications programming. This includes contributing to grant strategy, funder/donor relationships, and key communications deliverables in coordination with the Development and Communications teams.
* Lead or co\-lead select cross\-departmental strategic initiatives as assigned by the Executive Director.
* Other tasks as assigned by the Executive Director.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS**

* Minimum of four years in a senior management role including staff supervision, fundraising or finance, preferably in a nonprofit, business, or government agency.
* Success supervising and mentoring staff and supporting professional leadership development.
* Expertise in operational and strategic planning processes.
* Minimum one year experience as a community or labor organizer.
* BA or BS from a four\-year university, preferred.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills with exceptional attention to detail and experience as a spokesperson who can articulate messages to different audiences.
* Excellent interpersonal skills.
* Demonstrated commitment to social justice.
* Bilingual (Spanish/English) preferred.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
**TITLE:** Executive Director, Democratic Party of Arkansas

**POSITION ADMINISTRATIVE DATA:** Interested candidates should submit a cover letter, resume, and three references to careers@arkdems.org.

**REPORTS TO:** Chair, Democratic Party of Arkansas

**LOCATION:** Little Rock, Arkansas

**About the Opportunity:**

The Democratic Party of Arkansas (DPA) is seeking an Executive Director. In partnership with the Chair, the Executive Director is responsible for the strategy, activities, management, growth, and the day\-to\-day operations of the DPA. This specifically includes, but is not limited to, election\-based activities, fundraising, budgeting, staff recruitment and retention, communications, outreach, and building Party infrastructure. The position requires a commitment to work alongside the DPA Officers, Executive Committee, State Committee, elected officials, and candidates across the state. This position has a wide range of responsibilities, including serving as a trusted advisor to and strategic asset for the Chair of the Party, its elected and party officials, its candidates, and leaders across the state.

**ESSENTIAL JOB FUNCTIONS:**

● Serve as the chief strategic and tactical executive of the Democratic Party of Arkansas.

● Developing and implementing statewide campaign plans to win elections at the local, legislative, state, and federal levels.

● Overseeing the coordinated campaign efforts and coordination of consultants’ activities; assisting with the hiring of a coordinated campaign director during election years.

● Working with field personnel and state party staff to maintain and expand grassroots efforts and primary base through voter registration and volunteer recruitment.

● Manage relationships in\-state with elected officials, caucus leaders, candidates, auxiliaries, and state party membership; as well as national contacts through relationships at the ASDC and DNC, and partnerships with the DGA, DSCC, DCCC, and DLCC.

● Responsible for managing the day\-to\-day activities of all staff.

● Perform staff reviews, encourage staff development and training.

● Review and restructure staff functions and responsibilities as necessary.

● Direct fundraising efforts, develop strategy, and work with finance staff and/or consultants to implement.

● Work with the DPA Chair, DPA Treasurer, and staff to develop and adhere to the operating budget.

● Coordinate with DPA Secretary and Staff in preparing written reports for all meetings of the Executive and State Committees.

● Act as liaison with the staffs of the Democratic National Committee (DNC), the Association of State Democratic Committees (ASDC), and the Association of State Executive Directors.

● Attend DNC, ASDC, and county party meetings as necessary.

● Ensure all campaign finance reports, tax returns, and other required reports are accurately and timely filed by the compliance consultant.

● Work with the DPA Chair and Communications Director to issue press releases, speak on behalf of the Party where appropriate, and present the DPA in a positive and professional light.

● Oversee the State Party technology operations including database development and computer operations.

● Implement delegate selection process in presidential election cycles.

● Develop, oversee, and maintain relations with Democratic donors both in\-state and out\-of\-state.

● Develop training programs for the State Party, including party membership, campaign staff, and candidates.

● Oversee development and production of party\-building and message\-delivery tools, including but not limited to: newsletters, websites, email communications, social media, and brochures.

● Organize all meetings of the Executive and State Committees as required by the rules of the DPA.

● Maintain and work with legal counsel to ensure the DPA is in compliance with all state and federal law.

● Demonstrate an understanding of all aspects of elections, including state\-of\-the\-art campaign techniques, campaign planning, targeting, polling, election law, GOTV programs, party building, and pre\-election planning.

● Ensure building maintenance is adhered to for the DPA Headquarters.

**Highly qualified candidates must possess:**

● Substantial professional, nonprofit, business, or political senior management experience.

● Strong abilities in organization planning for strategy and program.

● Extensive team management skills with demonstrated ability to achieve high levels of performance and outcomes through management and influence.

● A reputation for leading with integrity and making decisions with the input of the appropriate stakeholders.

● Conflict and crisis\-management experience with proven, clear decision\-making ability.

● Demonstrated success in fundraising and knowledge of donor networks.

**Core competencies:**

● Clear, effective, high\-quality writer.

● Excellent in interpersonal skills and building relationships.

● Good information/administrative organizational skills.

● Digital by nature \- a natural with smartphone, iPad, tablet, and laptop for work and personal reasons; monitoring email and social media in real time is intuitive.

● Highly communicative \- responsive to internal and external requests, emails, and calls, within reason.

● Multi\-tasker \- Able to juggle multiple activities yet not lose focus on top priorities or let something slip through the cracks.

● Organized in thinking and doing.

● Committed to the values and practices of a diverse, equitable, and inclusive workplace with the ability to receive feedback and learn from it.

● Knowledge of Arkansas politics and the national political environment and developments.

● Willingness and flexibility to travel throughout Arkansas and out of state.

Pay: $80,000\.00 \- $85,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Life insurance
* Vision insurance

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
**Job Summary**


Plans, develops, implements, administers, evaluates, and monitors an aggressive direct fundraising program in a targeted geographical area including the service area of the Northwest Arkansas Area Command (NWAAC) under the direction of the Area Commander; develops and secures funds to achieve/surpass fundraising goals through a variety of financial development vehicles including: (1\) individual gifts and individual donor upgrading; (2\) corporate gifts and sponsorships; (3\) foundation support for specific programs and projects; (4\) direct mail appeals; (5\) government grants; and (5\) capital campaigns, and special events. Works directly and independently with local officers, their boards and committees to develop local promotional plans; plans and coordinates public relations activities and ensures compliance with the designated budget; confers directly with Divisional Headquarters administration and Boards as well as Territorial Headquarters when necessary.


**Fundraising \& Supervision** **(90%)**


Plans, develops, implements, administers, and sustains an aggressive financial development plan for Northwest Arkansas within the Arkansas\-Oklahoma Division; develops, plans, and conducts appropriate fundraising activities in support of the Area Command’s budget and programs; submits programs to the Area Commander for review, direction, and approval.


Solicits donations and cultivates relationships with donors in order to develop, secure, and maintain new income sources for present and long term financial support; ensures that all requests from donors and potential donors for information and clarification are responded to in an accurate, timely, and professional manner; evaluates day\-to\-day fundraising efforts to ensure that fundraising goals are met and or exceeded.


Performs both short and long\-term program planning and develops recommendations for enhancing financial development effectiveness; develops financial development goals for each program or activity and monitors progress to ensure goals are attained; establishes methods \& measures for monitoring \& evaluating fundraising goals and objectives; prepares an annual goal of dollars to be raised and gifts to be obtained for the fiscal year October 1st thru September 30th and submits the same for the Area Commander’s approval.


Develops and coordinates the operation of fundraising appeals; identifies new and innovative methods of increasing direct mail appeals; works closely with mail service firms to ensure productivity, effectiveness, and efficiency.


Plans, develops, and initiates a fundraising strategy to develop corporate gifts and sponsorships as well as foundation support for special programs and projects; researches financial status and philosophy or organizations to identify potential prospects for major gifts; contacts corporations to identify corporate representatives responsible for donor solicitation; cultivates and maintains an effective working relationship with corporate officials.


Maintains awareness of government legislation; reviews government publications to identify special funding available through government grants; obtains and completes grant applications to acquire funds; reviews and monitors grant stipulations and requirements to determine if the Salvation Army is eligible to receive funds; monitors the use of resulting funds to ensure compliance with government regulations.


Plans, develops, coordinates and monitors all details associated with the production of fundraising special events and campaigns; identifies the necessary resources, equipment, and personnel; plans event procedures and fundraising goals; recruits, motivates, and instructs volunteers and staff.


Plans, coordinates, and monitors public relations activities necessary to promote and conduct fundraising programs; develops printed materials such as brochures, flyers, posters, etc. and coordinates special mass mailings to the general public, prospects, and donors; plans and coordinates media advertisements including local television, radio and newspaper coverage; ensures that the image projected is in compliance with The Salvation Army standards and mission; evaluates appropriateness and effectiveness of public relations efforts.


Researches and analyzes the local market by conducting surveys and studies of the assigned geographical area to obtain and maintain awareness of the geographic and socio\-economic characteristics; determines appropriate fundraising vehicles and frequency of the same necessary to generate maximum level of donations and to meet/surpass established financial development goals.


Works with Commanding officers, their Boards and committees to develop local promotional plans; conducts presentations to the advisory boards.


Builds and maintains effective working relationships with professionals in the community; solicits and secures corporate sponsorships and major gifts as well as foundation support for The Salvation Army programs; maintains up\-to\-date and complete records regarding the same; ensures that corporations receive appropriate recognition and gratitude from The Salvation Army.


Develops, prepares and monitors regular financial reports illustrating financial development progress; established and maintains an organized and efficient donor record\-keeping system ensuring that accurate and complete records are prepared and maintained for each donor.


Develops the annual financial development program budget; administers the affairs of the position within the approved budget; prepares special financial reports as requested.


Assist the Commanding Officer in efforts to coordinate all program activities and services, and to advance the interests of the total Army program and strengthen the efforts of the officers and Advisory Board in developing and carrying on effective and relevant programs and services
